title: Smiling at 3:34 AM: Why Carlos Alcaraz Grinned After Losing
summary:
Imagine playing tennis until 3:34 in the morning. That's when Carlos Alcaraz's match finally ended at the US Open. He lost to Ben Shelton after four hours and 28 minutes — the latest finish in the tournament's history.

Most players would stomp off the court. Not Alcaraz. Cameras caught him walking through the tunnel with a giant grin on his face.

Why? Because five months earlier, he hurt his wrist so badly it hurt every single day. He missed the French Open and Wimbledon. He didn't even know if he could play in New York until one week before.

"I suffered, but I enjoyed," he said. "That's why I smiled when I walked out of the court, because I missed that feeling."

Alcaraz, 23, has won seven Grand Slam titles. But even he thinks these super-late matches are too much. "I think it's too much," he said. He wants matches to finish by 11pm.

Next up? He's playing for Team Europe at the Laver Cup in London. "When you have your team-mates, the best in the world, by your side," he said, "it's a weird feeling but it's beautiful."
why_it_matters: It shows that losing is not always the worst thing — getting back to something you love after being hurt or sick can be worth smiling about, just like coming back to school or a sport after a long break.

background_read: Carlos Alcaraz is a Spanish tennis star who became one of the youngest players ever to reach the top of the world rankings, and the US Open is one of tennis's four biggest tournaments, played every year in New York.
The Laver Cup is named after Rod Laver, a famous Australian tennis champion, and it works like a team sport: Team Europe plays against Team World.
Very late finishes at the US Open are a known problem — some other players have also complained that matches ending after midnight are too hard on everyone.
Article_Structure: WHO: Carlos Alcaraz, a 23-year-old tennis star with seven Grand Slam titles, and his opponent Ben Shelton
WHAT: Alcaraz lost a match that lasted four hours and 28 minutes and ended at 3:34 AM — the latest finish in US Open history — but he walked off with a big grin
WHERE: The US Open in New York; his next event is the Laver Cup in London
WHY: He smiled because a wrist injury had made him miss the French Open and Wimbledon, so he was just happy to be playing again

perspectives.description: They think his smile proves he truly loves tennis and is grateful just to play again after his injury.
They say a match ending at 3:34 AM is bad for the players' bodies and unfair to fans who have to go home and sleep.
They point out that long matches are exciting for TV but hard to schedule, so tournaments have to balance fun and fairness.
